spec.description: Is the machinery healthy: internal components, scheduled jobs, disk budget, containment, sensors and the engine process.

options.content: Everything that keeps detection running. If something on the Overview looks wrong, the cause is usually here.
The health manager checks every part and repairs what it can on its own.

spec.title: Component health
spec.description: Every internal component the health manager watches, with its state and self-repair attempts.

properties.value: Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy, Safe mode (running reduced), Recovery failed, or Retired.
Self-repair attempts in the current back-off window.

spec.title: Host load over time
spec.description: 0 Normal · 1 Resource pressure · 2 Conserving · 3 Critical.

options.content: Every enabled background job, as seen by the scheduler. Retired jobs drop out on their own.

spec.title: Scheduled jobs
spec.description: State, last success, runtime, time budget and trouble counts per job. Kills mean the job overran its budget and was stopped.

properties.value: Idle, Running, Paused (a more urgent job is running), or Waiting (due but held back).
Time since its last successful run (since the scheduler last started).
How long the last run took.
Longest it may actively run before being stopped.
Reported an error or exited abnormally.
Times it hit its time budget and was stopped.
Times it was paused so a more urgent job could run.
Scheduler ticks it waited because the host was under pressure.

options.content: The disk governor keeps the whole stack under a fixed size, trimming the oldest data first.

spec.title: Used vs budget (GB)
spec.description: Size of each stored data set against its budget, from the governor's last run.

spec.title: Budgets (GB)
spec.description: The limits those data sets are held to.

spec.title: Governor last success
spec.description: The governor runs on a schedule; this is how long ago it last succeeded.

options.content: What is being blocked or isolated right now, and whether blocking actions work.

spec.title: Devices tarpitted
spec.description: Devices trapped on the LAN by the ARP/NDP tarpit right now.

spec.title: Devices router-isolated
spec.description: Devices cut off from the internet at the router right now.

spec.title: Domains blocked
spec.description: Domains currently blocked in Pi-hole.

spec.title: Blocks waiting to retry
spec.description: Blocking commands that failed and are being retried. Anything here is not actually blocked yet.

spec.title: Blocks given up on
spec.description: Blocking commands that failed every retry. These domains are NOT blocked; check the Pi-hole connection.

spec.title: Blocking errors (per minute)
spec.description: Failures while executing a block, isolation or release, by integration. Should stay at 0.

spec.title: Processing delay
spec.description: Seconds between an event happening and the engine finishing it. A climbing value means it is falling behind.

spec.title: Events processed (per second)
spec.description: DNS and network events flowing through the engine. A drop to zero while devices are active means a sensor stalled.

spec.title: Threat intel loaded
spec.description: Have the threat-intel feeds loaded at least once? Until then every lookup reads as clean.

spec.title: Suricata scans OK (30 min)
spec.description: Share of Suricata scans that succeeded in the last 30 minutes (Suricata only runs during capture bursts).

spec.title: Evidence-graph export
spec.description: When the evidence graph was last published to Prometheus (every ~2 min). Stale means graph-based panels are stale.

spec.title: Engine CPU (100% = one full core)
spec.description: CPU used by the engine process.

spec.title: Engine memory
spec.description: Resident memory of the engine process. A steady climb with no plateau over days suggests a leak.

spec.title: Engine uptime
spec.description: Time since the engine last (re)started. Unexpected drops mean it crashed and was restarted.

spec.title: Unreadable model files removed
spec.description: Per-device ML model files found damaged at startup and removed (since the engine started). Each such device re-learns from scratch. Should stay 0; saves are atomic, so a non-zero value points at a disk problem.
